# 03. Experiments

Source: arXiv 2610.10447 article (sections 4, A–F) and the Perplexity blog.

## 3.1 Baselines

- **GRPO** — outcome-reward RL with a group-relative advantage (Shao et al., 2024).
- **OPSD** — on-policy self-distillation, teacher = student + privileged
  information, without separate teacher training (Zhao et al., 2026).
- **π-Distill** — jointly trains a privileged teacher and the student in a shared
  model, but the teacher's objective is different, and the student update is
  **off-policy** — it relies on trajectories generated by the teacher rather than
  the student's own generations (Penaloza et al., 2026).

Hyperparameters were tuned separately for each method; the selected configurations
were fixed before the comparison across several seeds.

## 3.2 Testbeds

| Benchmark | Base model | Teacher's privileged information |
|---|---|---|
| Numeric testbed | DeepSeek-V2-Lite | verified answer to the task |
| MATH | Qwen3-0.6B | detailed reference solution |
| LCBv6 (131 LiveCodeBench-V6 tasks) | Qwen3-8B | a successful sibling solution that passed all visible tests; otherwise the execution output (feedback) |
| AppWorld | Qwen3-4B-Instruct | summaries of previous attempts (skill bank) |
| Terminal-Bench 2.1 (trained on TMax) | Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct | private verifier information |

## 3.3 Main results

### Accuracy (Table 1) — mean ± std across runs

| Method | MATH (acc, %) | LCBv6 (acc, %) | AppWorld (state-test pass rate, %) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GRPO | 68.36 ± 3.73 | 46.13 ± 1.83 | 62.20 ± 2.83 |
| OPSD | 61.20 ± 2.10 | 45.34 ± 1.50 | 29.49 ± 2.48 |
| π-Distill | 42.25 ± 1.10 | 38.23 ± 1.72 | 59.85 ± 2.97 |
| **JOLT** | 72.14 ± 0.90 | 47.64 ± 1.10 | 51.92 ± 5.30 |
| **JOLT+** | **72.59 ± 1.17** | **49.08 ± 0.41** | **72.09 ± 6.01** |

Gain of JOLT+ over GRPO (the strongest baseline): numeric testbed **+1.5 pp**, MATH **+4.2 pp**,
LCBv6 **+3.0 pp**, AppWorld **+9.9 pp**, Terminal-Bench 2.1 pass@1 **+2.7 pp**
(per the article: +4.5 pp at pass@32).

### Terminal-Bench 2.1 (Table 2) — pass@k, %, one run per method

| Method | pass@1 | pass@4 | pass@16 | pass@32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base | 5.18 | 10.84 | 18.35 | 22.81 |
| GRPO | 8.25 | 17.04 | 26.91 | 30.34 |
| OPSD | 2.82 | 6.96 | 13.59 | 16.90 |
| π-Distill | 4.99 | 10.50 | 18.30 | 22.31 |
| **JOLT** | 6.56 | 13.56 | 22.06 | 25.69 |
| **JOLT+** | **10.96** | **20.12** | **29.99** | **34.83** |

JOLT without a direct student reward trails GRPO at this longest horizon, but
outperforms the base model and both distillation baselines at all $k$; JOLT+ is
the best at every $k$.

### Consistency across runs (Table 4)

Probability that JOLT+ improves over GRPO at the final checkpoint (all pairs of runs):

| Testbed | JOLT+ runs | GRPO runs | P(improvement), % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Numeric testbed | 5 | 4 | 90.0 |
| MATH | 3 | 3 | 88.9 |
| LCBv6 | 3 | 3 | 100.0 |
| AppWorld | 3 | 3 | 100.0 |
| Mean (equal weights) | — | — | **94.7** |

95% percentile bootstrap interval for the mean: [83.3 %, 100.0 %].

## 3.4 Token efficiency

Comparison at equal accuracy **63.44 %** on MATH (the GRPO checkpoint at the
"knee" of the training curve; for JOLT, the inverse of the fitted curve):

| Counter | GRPO, M tokens | JOLT, M tokens | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Completion tokens | 8.04 | 0.617 | **13.0×** |
| Processed training tokens | 8.40 | 1.30 | **6.5×** |

Over the target accuracy range of 55–65 %: JOLT spends **9.5–14.4× fewer**
completion tokens and **4.3–7.4× fewer** processed tokens.

Fitted sigmoids $a(B) = a_0 + \frac{a_\infty - a_0}{1 + (B_{50}/B)^k}$:

| Counter | Method | $a_\infty$, % | $B_{50}$ | $k$ | RMSE, pp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completion | GRPO | 70.044 | 4.173 | 1.655 | 0.994 |
| Completion | OPSD | 61.706 | 0.512 | 2.076 | 0.938 |
| Completion | JOLT | 72.123 | 0.440 | 2.413 | 1.126 |
| Processed | GRPO | 70.441 | 4.343 | 1.501 | 0.959 |
| Processed | OPSD | 61.691 | 1.314 | 2.270 | 0.937 |
| Processed | JOLT | 72.125 | 0.955 | 2.634 | 1.152 |

The overall picture: OPSD learns quickly at small budgets but plateaus at ~62 %;
GRPO learns more slowly but keeps growing to ~70 %; JOLT is fast at the start and
reaches the highest ceiling (~72 %).

## 3.5 Ablations of the teacher objective (Appendix C, MATH, step 75)

| Configuration | Student reward | Teacher reward | Teacher KL | LR | Held-out acc, % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OPSD | — | — | — | 2×10⁻⁶ | 62.95 ± 0.78 |
| OPSD + Student Reward | ✓ | — | — | 2×10⁻⁶ | 66.52 ± 0.73 |
| JOLT (teacher KL only) | — | — | ✓ | 1×10⁻⁶ | 65.39 ± 0.97 |
| JOLT (teacher outcome only) | — | ✓ | — | 2×10⁻⁶ | 67.87 ± 0.86 |
| **JOLT (full objective)** | — | ✓ | ✓ | 2×10⁻⁶ | **72.10 ± 0.82** |
| **JOLT+ (full objective)** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 2×10⁻⁶ | **73.80 ± 0.74** |

Conclusions: explicit optimization of the teacher gives a gain over OPSD; the
combination "student reward + distillation" (66.52) is noticeably weaker than the
full JOLT+ objective (73.80) — the gain comes precisely from training the teacher,
not only from adding the student reward.

## 3.6 Gradient analysis (Appendix E)

- GRPO: the error is dominated by **variance**.
- OPSD: low variance, but a **growing empirical bias** over the course of training.
- JOLT / JOLT+: retain low variance and a noticeably smaller bias than OPSD.

Reference — a Monte-Carlo estimate of the reward gradient: an average of 8
independent REINFORCE estimates over 512 completions per task; $K=32$ independent
estimates of the student gradient in each batch of 8 tasks; intervals — 95 %
pointwise band-bootstrap over 100,000 paired resamples.

The authors' caveats: these measurements do not isolate the effect of teacher
training, do not establish reward-consistency of the full joint update, and depend
on the gradient scale. Direction (cosine-like metrics) is checked separately: there,
the distillation-only and combined estimates show a smaller spread of directions
and a higher mean cosine similarity with the reference than reward-only.

## 3.7 Teacher–student agreement (Appendix D)

Comparison of teacher and student log-probabilities on the same prefix (red — the
teacher's probability is higher, blue — lower):

- under OPSD the divergence is spread across most of the answer;
- under JOLT/JOLT+ the differences are **smaller** and concentrated in **fewer
  token positions**;
- this matches the lower aggregate KL over the course of training.

## 3.8 Hyperparameters (Table 3)

$B$ is the number of tasks per update, $G$ is the group size per active role.
On the numeric testbed and MATH, JOLT/JOLT+ use 4 teacher rollouts and 4 student
rollouts per task, whereas GRPO and OPSD use 8 student rollouts.

| Group size $G$ | 8 | 8 | 8 | 4 | 32 |

## 3.9 Evaluation protocols

### Numeric testbed

Official train/test splits: 7,473 / 1,319 tasks. Training: temperature 1.0, top-p
1.0, maximum sequence length 8,192 tokens, completion limit 4,096 tokens.
Evaluation: one greedy completion per test task.

### MATH

Full official splits: 7,500 / 5,000 tasks. Training and evaluation: temperature 1.0,
top-p 1.0, completion limit 16,384 tokens. Evaluation: one completion **without
privileged information**, thinking disabled.

### LCBv6

131 tasks from LiveCodeBench v6 (released between February and April 2025). For each
task, ~50 % of the private upstream tests are randomly chosen as visible during
training (NumPy seed 0) — 2,421 visible cases, 2,431 held out. Evaluation uses the
full set of 4,852 tests for the same tasks, including the held-out ones. 4 student
completions are generated per task; temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95; prompt and response
limits — 2,048 and 8,192 tokens.

### AppWorld

Training on all 90 public train tasks. Evaluation — 57 tasks of the official dev
split, every 25 updates. At a checkpoint: one student trajectory per task per seed,
greedy decoding, context limit 65,536 tokens, maximum 50 turns. Metric — state-test
pass rate (the fraction of passed state tests, averaged over tasks). The roles use
an adapted one-shot ReAct skeleton.

### Terminal-Bench

Training on TMax (50 updates), evaluation on the full Terminal-Bench 2.1 set.
Harness — mini-SWE-agent (Vanillux2Agent) with a persistent shell. Temperature 0.7,
top-p 0.95, limit of 16,384 tokens per assistant turn, maximum 64 agent steps,
bash command timeout 120 s. The **student without privileged information** is
evaluated. 128 trajectories are sampled per task; pass@k for $k\in\{1,4,16,32\}$
by the estimator of Chen et al. (2021).

## 3.10 Run statistics

- Table 1: 3 runs per configuration, except π-Distill on LCBv6 — 5.
- Numeric testbed evaluation: 4 runs for GRPO/OPSD/π-Distill, 5 for JOLT/JOLT+.
- Other experiments: 5 seeds, normal-approximation 95 % CI (mean ± 1.96 SE).
- Terminal-Bench and gradient analysis — one run per method.
- EMA smoothing is applied only to training curves, not to the tabular totals.
